layers.note: An introduced herb of prairies, lawns, roadsides and disturbed open ground.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −3 °C, gone by −8 °C, up to about 14 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Lows to about −26 °C borne, gone below about −34 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warmest-month means from about 13 to 25 °C, gone below 10 °C and above 29 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 2,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 900 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 500.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.35, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; naturalised under summer-dry and summer-wet temperate climates to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Hairy cat's ear, from Europe, is naturalised in mild temperate climates, abundant on the Pacific coast (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
